name: Speed parade - every movement rate, side by side
notes: A pure demonstration, not a rule proof: the owner asked to see units of different speeds moving side by side, so this lines up one of every mobile unit type from both rosters on a common starting column, all walking the same distance toward a lone static Grid Nexus, fastest at the top and slowest at the bottom. The target is a Nexus rather than a barracks on purpose - at 400 HP it outlasts the fastest arrivals long enough for the slower ones to actually get there too, rather than the demonstration ending the moment the first few units bring a 120-HP barracks down; its destruction still ends the Pulse if the parade runs long enough; pulseTicks is sized well past the slowest unit's crossing either way. Nothing here is a canon claim - movement rates on the fixture rosters are disposable bench content (AGENTS.md Section 2), tuned freely. Two changes made for this scenario also apply everywhere: the citizen trooper and marksman moved from 3/4 (16 ticks/step) to 1/1 (12 ticks/step) - the owner's other finding, that initial movement felt a little slow, and troopers/marksmen are the units most players spend the most time watching. Order, fastest to slowest at the rates now in play among the units that actually move: slinger/runner/scav (3 ticks/step, tied - the third speed pass, 2026-08-23, closed a gap that used to separate them), worker/trooper/marksman (4, tied), raider (5), fuelwagon (6), hauler (8) - arriving in that order and then settling into whatever each one's weapon does to the Nexus. "Actually move" is doing real work in that sentence: scav and worker are both flee-behaviour, and their only hostile here is the Nexus itself, which has no attack - selectTarget (perception.ts) never gives a flee-behaviour unit an unarmed target, so both have stood still at their spawn tile since this fixture was first authored, unrelated to any speed pass. Worth knowing before reading the parade as one race rather than seven movers and two spectators.
